head: 767de7b04f90c562d775f515f382e40d016556ce
label: task147-outbox-relay-marksent-pairability
purpose: correct TASK-146 evidence wording (lockHoldMs endpoint excludes the trailing summary; a caught unlock() error is not proof of release; 1571 is an observed peak) and, in an isolated scratch MySQL with the real mapper wiring, prove or disprove ONE test-only, target-call-limited instrumentation candidate for the per-call markSent lower-layer wall clock. No production plugin, no DataSource swap, no markSent optimization, no defaults changed, no large load.

verdict.reason: The one candidate (a test-only MyBatis StatementHandler.update interceptor filtered by MappedStatement.id == ...VerifyEventOutboxMapper.markSent, registered ONLY on the IT's own SqlSessionFactory) pairs one target call to exactly one lower-layer sample on real scratch MySQL with the real mapper annotation SQL, with non-target isolation, zero readings when off, ordered consecutive pairing, failure-exception type unchanged, scope cleanup, auto-commit visibility, update row counts, final state and connection release all equal to the no-probe baseline. This proves the LAYER is pairable in isolation; it does NOT prove the production Spring/Hikari assembly, does NOT locate a production bottleneck, and does NOT show any throughput gain.

nextSingleFactor.factor: per-row markSent internal cost composition (connection acquire / client JDBC execute / commit / server-side SQL / remaining client wait)
nextSingleFactor.measuredLayer: client JDBC statement execution wall clock (PreparedStatement.execute() + getUpdateCount()), pairing ONE call to ONE sample
nextSingleFactor.observedInThisLayer: not measured here (no load); this task only proves the layer can be paired and does not change semantics
nextSingleFactor.stillUnknown: separating connection acquire, explicit commit, and server-side SQL vs network round trip; and the same pairing under the production Spring/Hikari wiring (no verify-service Spring-context真库 IT precedent was introduced)
nextSingleFactor.boundary: the lower-layer reading is a client JDBC call wall clock; it must NOT be called pure server-side SQL, pure fsync, pure pool wait, or commit time

item1_lockHoldEndpoint.was: lockHoldMs includes the summary output (report wrote 'summary output + unlock')
item1_lockHoldEndpoint.now: lockHoldMs endpoint is taken AFTER the unlock() call returns (or throws and is caught) and BEFORE the summary log is printed: includes the unlock call, EXCLUDES the trailing summary output
item1_lockHoldEndpoint.codeTruth: holdStart -> processingNanos (end of batch loop, before finally) -> finally { unlock() ; if (completed && diagEnabled) lockHoldNanos = nanoTime - holdStart; log.info(summary) }

item2_unlockFailure.now: a caught unlock() error does not prove the lock was actually released, so the elapsed time must NOT be called a 'full hold' or taken as proof of release; renamed to the post-unlock timing segment

item3_backlogPeak.now: unchanged: 1571 is the observed peak after the FIRST sample @2026-09-27 00:38:08.935; the first sample is later than load end, so the real peak between 00:37:41 and 00:38:08 is UNKNOWN (>= 1571)

assemblyReview.relayTransaction: VerifyOutboxRelay.relay() has NO @Transactional; each markSent/incrRetry is an independent auto-commit call

candidate.kind: test-only MyBatis plugin on StatementHandler.update, filtered by MappedStatement.id
candidate.registeredOnlyIn: the IT's own MybatisConfiguration via configuration.addInterceptor(new MarkSentProbe())
candidate.pairingMethod: one target statement execution queues exactly one sample into a THREAD-LOCAL slot; the IT clears then calls then drains; single-threaded so one markSent <-> one sample
candidate.measurableClientBoundary: PreparedStatement.execute() + getUpdateCount() wall clock; sample also carries rows (update count) and a failed flag
notMeasurable: splitting server-side SQL execution from network round trip
candidate.nonTargetIsolation: id != TARGET_ID -> proceed without queueing; selectPendingBatch/incrRetry produce no sample
candidate.switch: thread-local ENABLED; when off, zero nanoTime sampling
candidate.exceptionCleanup: try/catch/finally; on failure queues one sample failed=true rows=-1 and rethrows; scope cleaned via thread-local, no cross-talk into the next call
